summary: Metering rounding delta between embedding and chat aggregation causing small invoice variance
description: Issue summary: Customer BrightCall reports a small but recurring variance (0.3-1.2 USD) on their monthly invoice where the line item labeled 'inference: embeddings' plus 'inference: chat' summed by the customer does not match the invoice total we generated. Impact: Small financial variance for accounting reconciliation; customer requests explanation and closing of the gap to prevent repeated disputes. Observed vs expected: BrightCall's internal aggregation of per-endpoint usage (embeddings + chat sessions) yields a different token total after rounding/aggregation than Redwood's billed total. Timeframe: discrepancies observed on invoices dated 2026-02-28 and 2026-03-01 (billing window 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer exported per-endpoint hourly usage (CSV) for the period 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28 from their dashboard. 2) They summed token counts for rwd-embed-1 and rwd-chat-3b, then applied published per-unit rates. 3) Compared that local total to the invoice line items and found a delta of $0.36 (Feb invoice) and $0.89 (Mar preliminary). 4) Customer confirmed no subaccount cross-posting and single billing org.
logs_excerpt: 2026-02-28T23:58:12Z usage-postback: org=brightcall endpoint=embed token_count=12345.4 postback_id=pbk_8f3c; 2026-02-28T23:58:13Z usage-postback: org=brightcall endpoint=chat token_count=9876.6 postback_id=pbk_8f3d; aggregator: hourly_bucket us-east 2026-02-28T23:00 -> total_tokens=22222.0 computed_billed_units=22222 rounding_strategy=ceil
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: rounding strategy differences between raw postbacks (fractional tokens from streaming) and the billing aggregation (per-hour bucket rounding or per-request rounding). Query run against usage DB shows we store fractional token counts at ingestion but billing pipeline applies 'ceil' at per-hour per-endpoint bucket for dedicated customers in us-east to preserve revenue guardrails. Found two consumer postbacks with identical request IDs that were retried within 2s window and de-duplicated at ingestion, but rounding applied before de-dupe in one legacy path. Related: linked SUP-30192 flagged a similar hourly-window split affecting reserved hours. Next steps: patch billing transform to apply rounding consistently at final aggregation stage and create backfill for affected hours. Low-impact work-around offered: apply manual adjustment credit on current invoice while patch is scheduled.
